infra.monitoring.title: Monitoring
infra.monitoring.subtitle: CloudWatch metrics and alarms for the current context
infra.monitoring.partial: partial data — AWS has not finished aggregating this window
infra.monitoring.noProfile: No AWS profile selected. Pick one on the Accounts tab, or on the context bar at the top of the page.
infra.monitoring.badWindow: The time window is invalid: the end must be after the start.
infra.monitoring.tooManySeries: Too many series in one load.
infra.monitoring.sidecarUnavailable: The engine is not available — monitoring needs the desktop app.
infra.monitoring.notLoaded: Nothing loaded yet. Pick a resource and a time range, then press Load.
infra.monitoring.reloadHint: Bypasses the cache — this pays for the same window twice.
infra.monitoring.zeroCost: nothing charged — every series came from cache
infra.monitoring.window.label: Window
infra.monitoring.window.dirty: Selected {selected} but still showing {shown} — press Load
infra.monitoring.window.sendToLogsHint: Carries this exact window to the Logs tab
infra.monitoring.target.heading: Resource
infra.monitoring.target.notLoaded: List not loaded — press the refresh button next to it
infra.monitoring.target.reloadWhy: List this account's resources: ECS services, load balancers, databases, queues and instances. Read-only commands.
infra.monitoring.legend.hint: p50 / p95 / p99 are one hue in three shades — read the label at the end of each line, not the colour.
infra.monitoring.alarm.title: Alarms
infra.monitoring.alarm.truncated: Showing the first page — there are more alarms.
infra.monitoring.alarm.dragHint: Drag the handle on the chart to set the threshold.
infra.monitoring.alarm.name: Alarm name
infra.monitoring.alarm.actionsHint: Comma-separated SNS topic ARNs, up to 5.
infra.monitoring.alarm.confirmAction: Create or update a CloudWatch alarm
infra.monitoring.alarm.none: No alarms configured for this chart.
infra.monitoring.ask.title: Monitoring
infra.monitoring.ask.spike: What happened in this window that pushed latency up?
infra.monitoring.ask.week: Compare this window with the same window a week ago.
infra.monitoring.ask.incident: Walk me through the firing alarms and what caused them.
infra.monitoring.target.required: Pick a resource before loading — CloudWatch returns no series when the query is not filtered to one.
infra.monitoring.empty.title: Pick a resource to watch
infra.monitoring.empty.hint: The charts follow the kind of resource you pick — an ECS service shows CPU/memory/running tasks, a load balancer shows calls and latency, a queue shows depth and oldest message age. Press the refresh button beside the picker if the list is still empty.
infra.monitoring.alarm.otherCount: {n} more alarms elsewhere in the account
infra.monitoring.logErrors.title: Errors in application logs
infra.monitoring.logErrors.needGroups: We do not know where this resource writes its logs yet. Press Find — it only reads configuration and costs nothing.
infra.monitoring.logErrors.guessed: These log groups were matched by NAME, not read from configuration — the list may be incomplete. A zero here does not prove there were no errors.
infra.monitoring.logErrors.confirmAction: Run CloudWatch Logs Insights to count error lines
infra.monitoring.logErrors.confirmCost: This run scans about {gb} GB, roughly {usd} USD. Insights bills by bytes scanned — unlike the metric charts above.
infra.monitoring.logErrors.queryFailed: The Insights query ended with status {status}.
infra.monitoring.logErrors.timeout: The query ran too long and we stopped following it. Try a shorter time range.
infra.monitoring.logErrors.failed: Could not count errors in the logs
infra.monitoring.logErrors.found: {n} error lines, {k} distinct, in the last {span}
infra.monitoring.logErrors.clean: No error lines in the last {span}
infra.monitoring.logErrors.partial: Some log groups could not be read, so this list is incomplete: {err}
infra.monitoring.logErrors.tooMany: Too many lines to fetch them all — these are the most recent, so the count above is a floor.
infra.monitoring.logErrors.countTitle: Count errors over time (costs a scan)
infra.monitoring.logErrors.countWhy: The section above reads the most recent error lines and bills per request, so it is cheap. This one charts error counts over time with CloudWatch Logs Insights, which bills by bytes scanned — so it asks first.
infra.monitoring.target.failed: Could not list resources — see the error below
infra.monitoring.target.engineMismatch: The running engine is an older build and does not understand this request. Restart AWOG to load the new engine.
infra.monitoring.target.denied: The current role is missing: {actions}. The list below is therefore built from existing alarms and is incomplete; a full list needs cloudwatch:ListMetrics, while log groups only need logs:DescribeLogGroups.
infra.monitoring.logErrors.dropped: Dropped {n} lines that declare themselves INFO/DEBUG — the CloudWatch filter matches substrings, so it catches those too.
